title: How to Create a Full Funnel Advertising Strategy That Works
summary: Read our step-by-step guide to full-funnel advertising. Learn how to allocate budget, build audience segments, choose channels, and measure performance.
body_markdown:
**A full-funnel advertising strategy connects awareness, consideration, conversion, and retention campaigns under** **one system** : shared audiences, consistent creative, and a single measurement framework, rather than running each stage as a disconnected campaign. You build one in eight steps: map your funnel stages, audit your existing data, allocate budget by stage, define audience segments, build a creative framework, choose channels, connect the stages with a shared data feedback loop, and set stage-specific KPIs.


Most guides on this topic tell you to “balance your funnel.” What they don’t tell you is that the top and bottom of the funnel aren’t starving; both are getting more budget than before. It’s **the stage after the sale that’s quietly being defunded** , and that’s the crack breaking most “full-funnel” strategies before they get the chance to prove themselves. Read more on that below.


Key Highlights


- **A full-funnel advertising strategy is one connected system** across TOFU, MOFU, BOFU, and post-purchase retention, not four separate campaigns run by four separate teams and tools.
- Gartner’s CMO Spend Survey found awareness and conversion now claim **62.6% of total media spend** (up over 10% since 2024), while loyalty and retention spend has fallen **29% to under 15%** , the real budget gap breaking full-funnel strategies this year.
- Full-funnel advertisers who connect the stages see it in the numbers: Krungthai Bank paired programmatic DOOH awareness with mobile retargeting and posted a **1.43% CTR** (vs. a 0.70% benchmark) and a **40% lift in brand image** .


## What is a Full Funnel Advertising Strategy?


**A full-funnel advertising strategy is the practice of planning, buying, and measuring advertising across every stage of the buyer’s journey: awareness, consideration, conversion, and retention, as one connected system rather than as isolated, stage-by-stage campaigns.**


It’s a narrower term than the[full marketing funnel](https://perion.com/glossary/marketing-funnel/) , which also covers organic search, product experience, sales, and CRM. **A full-funnel advertising strategy is specifically about paid media** : the same audience data, creative logic, and measurement stack carried across every stage you’re buying media against, from a Digital Out-of-Home impression a stranger sees on their commute to the retargeting ad they see after abandoning a cart.


### Why Full Funnel Advertising Works (And Why Most Advertisers Skip It)


It works because **unconnected stages compete with themselves.** When BOFU runs alone, it’s bidding on the same shrinking pool of high-intent, already-searching users as every competitor, and that pool gets more expensive every quarter. **A connected TOFU stage keeps refilling that pool and can become increasingly expensive and competitive. A connected TOFU stage keeps introducing people to the brand before they reach the point of conversion, giving BOFU campaigns a broader pool of known prospects to work with rather than relying solely on users already searching for a solution** **.** ****


The part most advertisers skip isn’t awareness or conversion; both are already well-funded. According to[Gartner’s CMO Spend Survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-06-08-gartner-marketing-survey-finds-awareness-and-conversion-account-for-62-6-of-total-media-spend) , **awareness and conversion together now account for 62.6% of total media spend** , a jump of more than 10 percentage points since 2024. Over the same period, spend on **customer loyalty and retention fell 29%, to under 15% of the total** . That’s the stage most “full-funnel” plans drop once the media plan is built, which means the funnel isn’t balanced; it’s been squeezed into a barbell shape, heavy on both ends and thin in the parts that carry a customer from a single sale into a repeat one.


A strategy only pays off when the stages are wired together, not just budgeted together.[Perion’s own research with Advertiser Perceptions](https://perion.com/blog/despite-gains-cmos-still-struggle-to-prove-value-to-cfos-finds-new-research-from-perion-and-advertiser-perceptions) points to the same measurement gap: only 23% of marketers currently have a unified measurement system in place, while marketers using unified performance systems report stronger collaboration with finance, stronger business outcomes, and greater confidence in demonstrating marketing’s ROI. **** The research reinforces the cost of fragmented measurement: when data and performance insights remain spread across platforms, marketers have less visibility into how activity across the customer journey contributes to business outcomes. **** **** That’s the operating gap[Perion One](https://perion.com/platform/) is built to close: **one system to plan, activate, and read performance across every stage** instead of stitching results together from four separate platforms after the fact.


## Step 1: Map Your Funnel Stages


Skip the generic “awareness = top, sales = bottom” definitions. In an advertising plan, each stage needs its own objective, its own audience logic, and its own success metric. In practice, it looks like this:


### Top of Funnel: Awareness


**Objective:** expand qualified reach and build brand memory structures among people who aren’t in-market yet.


**What it looks like:** a CTV and Digital Out-of-Home push in category-relevant contexts – an insurer running DOOH near pharmacies during flu season, for example, with no direct-response CTA. The job is exposure and recall, not clicks.


**Measured by:**[ad recall](https://perion.com/glossary/ad-recall/) , reach, frequency, and brand lift.


### Middle of Funnel: Consideration


**Objective:** convert people who’ve been exposed but aren’t yet convinced into a trackable, engaged pool.


**What it looks like:** retargeting audiences who showed real intent, high CTV completion rates, or meaningful time spent on a product page, with a proof-driven display or social sequence, built dynamically by Outmax and personalized through Adaptive Creative.


**Measured by:** engagement rate, video completion, content downloads, cost per lead.


### Bottom of Funnel: Conversion


**Objective:** close the decision for users who’ve already shown clear intent.


**What it looks like:**[search engines](https://perion.com/channels/search-engines/) plus retargeting to cart abandoners with an offer-led message and a single CTA.


**Measured by:**[conversion rate](https://perion.com/glossary/conversion-rate/) ,[ROAS](https://perion.com/glossary/return-on-ad-spend-roas/) , customer acquisition cost.


### Post-Purchase: Retention


**Objective:** turn a one-time buyer into a repeat one, and reduce how hard paid acquisition has to work to hit revenue targets.


**What it looks like:** a CRM-fed audience of recent customers served a loyalty or cross-sell campaign a set number of days after purchase, on the same platform used to run acquisition media, not bolted onto a separate email tool nobody else on the team can see.


**Measured by:** repeat purchase rate,[lifetime value](https://perion.com/glossary/lifetime-value-clv/) , and retention’s share of total media budget, the metric that is currently getting squeezed below 15% industry-wide.


## Step 2: Audit Your Data Before You Allocate a Single Dollar


Before a single dollar moves, check five things:


- **First-party data coverage by stage.**[First-party data](https://perion.com/glossary/first-party-data/) quality directly limits how well you can target and measure each stage: audit what you have, not what you assume you have.
- **Historical performance by stage,** not blended CAC or blended ROAS. A blended number hides whether TOFU, MOFU, or BOFU is the actual weak link.
- **Existing creative inventory mapped to stage.** Most brands discover they have dozens of BOFU-style assets and almost nothing built for awareness.
- **Attribution setup.** Can you see a user move from an impression to a click to a sale, or does every channel report its own, incomparable version of credit?
- **Whether there’s a shared activation layer,** like a[customer data platform](https://perion.com/glossary/customer-data-platform-cdp/) , or whether each channel is siloed with its own audience definitions.


A quick gut check: if your only retention data point is “email open rate,” you don’t have a retention audience; you have a distribution list.


## Step 3: Spread Your Budget Across the Funnel


Don’t copy an industry benchmark ratio wholesale; use the audit from Step 2 to find where your funnel is actually leaking. **High reach but flat branded search volume points to an underfunded TOFU.** **Strong branded search but weak conversion points to a BOFU or creative problem,** not a budget problem.


Most advertisers are already over-indexed on TOFU and BOFU. Before adding more budget to either, check whether retention is the real gap. For example, a mid-market retailer with a predictable repeat-purchase cycle might deliberately ring-fence a defined share of its media budget for retention, rather than letting it get absorbed back into acquisition whenever a quarter gets tight.[Gartner’s CMO Spend Survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-06-08-gartner-marketing-survey-finds-awareness-and-conversion-account-for-62-6-of-total-media-spend) found that loyalty and retention spending had fallen to less than 15% of total media spend, while the most AI-mature organisations allocated a larger share to these activities.


Once you’ve set a working split,[our guide to the ROI of full-funnel advertising](https://perion.com/blog/what-is-the-roi-of-full-funnel-advertising/) walks through how to calculate the return each stage is generating, so you can defend or adjust the split with numbers.


## Step 4: Define Your Audience Segments for Each Stage


Each stage needs an audience built on a different kind of signal, not just a narrower version of the same list.


- **TOFU:** contextual targeting and[lookalike modeling](https://perion.com/glossary/lookalike-modeling/) off your best existing customers, kept broad, not narrowed by conversion signals that don’t exist yet for these users.
- **MOFU:** engagement-based pools: video completers, multi-page site visitors, content downloaders, built and refreshed through a shared data layer.
- **BOFU:** high-intent search terms, cart abandoners, and pricing-page visitors.
- **Retention:** the existing customer list, segmented by purchase recency and frequency, synced from CRM into the same activation layer as acquisition audiences; so retention isn’t run through a disconnected tool nobody else on the media team can see.


## Step 5: Build Your Creative Framework


**Keep the same brand codes, logo treatment, color, and tone across every stage, and let the message intensity, not the brand, change as the audience gets closer to a decision** .


- **Top of Funnel Creative** – **Emotional, sensory, brand-forward, minimal copy** , and built to work with the sound off on CTV and DOOH. For example, a 15-second spot that leads with a visual brand cue before any product shot appears.
- **Middle of Funnel Creative** – **Proof-driven: testimonials, comparisons, use cases** . A slightly longer format is fine here, but the CTA should still nudge, not close.
- **Bottom of Funnel Creative** – **Direct offer, urgency, one clear CTA, visible price or promo** . Perion’s[Adaptive Creative](https://perion.com/platform/advertisers/adaptive-creative/) and[dynamic creative optimization](https://perion.com/glossary/dynamic-creative-optimization/) let this messaging shift automatically as performance data comes in, rather than waiting on a manual creative refresh.


## Step 6: Choose Your Channels and Configure Each Stage


The same channel can serve two different stages; what changes is the bid strategy, audience, and creative attached to it.


**Top of funnel channels:**[CTV](https://perion.com/channels/ctv/) ,[DOOH](https://perion.com/channels/dooh/) ,[Audio](https://perion.com/channels/audio/) .


**Middle of funnel channels:**[YouTube](https://perion.com/channels/youtube/) ,[Meta](https://perion.com/channels/meta/) ,[TikTok](https://perion.com/channels/tiktok/) ,[Websites](https://perion.com/channels/websites/) .


**Bottom of funnel channels:**[Search Engines](https://perion.com/channels/search-engines/) , plus retargeting on Websites and social.


A Meta prospecting campaign and a Meta retargeting campaign are, functionally, two different channels wearing the same logo; configure and budget them separately.

## Step 7: Connect the Stages With a Data Feedback Loop


Most full-funnel campaigns share a budget spreadsheet. Few share a nervous system.


Without a feedback loop, each funnel stage runs on stale assumptions. Top-of-funnel (TOFU) prospecting keeps targeting people who have already converted. Bottom-of-funnel (BOFU) conversion data sits in a dashboard instead of shaping who gets targeted next. The stages coexist. They don’t communicate.


A connected setup closes that gap in two directions. BOFU conversion data feeds back upstream to seed TOFU lookalike audiences, sharpening prospecting with signals from people who actually bought. TOFU and middle-of-funnel (MOFU) exposure data flows the other way, suppressing spending on anyone who has already converted. A customer who just bought stops seeing a prospecting ad for the same product the next day.


Intelligence without activation is just reporting. The value is in the loop closing automatically, in near real time, without a strategist manually pulling exports and re-uploading audience lists between platforms.


## Step 8: Set Up KPIs for Full Funnel Performance Measurement


None of the previous seven steps mean anything if you’re judging every stage by the same metric; a TOFU campaign measured on conversion rate will always look like it’s failing, even when it’s working exactly as designed.


- **Platform-level attribution:** understand what each walled garden reports on its own, and where that reporting is structurally biased toward that platform.
- **Cross-channel attribution:** a multi-touch model spanning every stage, not a last-click view that hands 100% of the credit to whichever channel closed the sale.
- **Brand lift measurement:** a recurring cadence of studies for TOFU, not a one-off test run once a year.
- **Incrementality testing:** holdout groups that prove media is causing the lift, not just correlating with it.


**The KPI framework at a glance**


**Stage** **Primary KPI** **Review Cadence** **Typically Owned By**


TOFU Ad recall, brand lift, incremental reach Monthly / quarterly Brand team


MOFU Engagement rate, CPL, funnel velocity Weekly Growth/lifecycle team


BOFU Conversion rate, ROAS, CAC Daily / weekly Performance team


Retention Repeat purchase rate, LTV, retention share of budget Monthly CRM/lifecycle team


For the ROI math behind each of these KPIs, see[our full guide to full-funnel advertising ROI](https://perion.com/blog/what-is-the-roi-of-full-funnel-advertising/) .


## 6 Full Funnel Advertising Mistakes That Kill Campaigns


Most of these aren’t strategy failures; they’re the same funnel built correctly on paper, then quietly undone by how it’s actually run day to day.


1. **Treating TOFU as a vanity-metrics exercise.** Reach and impressions with no downstream tracking means you can never prove or disprove that awareness spend is doing anything.
2. **Letting retention get absorbed back into acquisition.** It’s the first line item cut when a quarter gets tight, which is exactly how it ends up under 15% of budget industry-wide.
3. **Running BOFU creative at the top of the funnel.** A hard offer-led ad shown to someone who has never heard of the brand reads as spam rather than an introduction.
4. **Keeping stage-level teams and tools siloed.** If the TOFU team and the BOFU team use different platforms and never see each other’s data, there is no funnel, just four campaigns that happen to run at once.
5. **Crediting 100% of a sale to the last click.** Then cutting the upper-funnel media that quietly made that last click possible, based on flawed attribution.
6. **Setting the funnel up once and never feeding data back upstream.** See Step 7; without that loop, “full-funnel” is really just four separate funnels sharing a budget line.


## Case Study: Krungthai Bank


Krungthai Bank needed to differentiate itself from its competitors in the digital investment space, with a single objective: an omnichannel campaign that delivered high engagement, strong viewability, and measurable brand impact.


**The bank used a dual-layered approach to drive mobile app adoption** : programmatic DOOH for mass awareness across high-traffic urban locations (TOFU), then device IDs captured from that exposure were retargeted with precise mobile ads (BOFU), using geofencing around Krungthai Bank and competitor branches, dayparting toward peak engagement windows, and frequency management to avoid ad fatigue.


The connected approach delivered a **1.43% overall CTR** against a 0.70% benchmark, over 8,000 clicks, an **83% viewability rate** , and a **40% uplift in positive brand image** as measured by Happydemics. ## FAQs


### What is the ideal budget split for a full-funnel advertising strategy?


There isn’t one universal ratio; the right split comes out of the audit in Step 2, not a benchmark applied blindly. If you want a data-backed starting point and the math behind adjusting it,[our guide to full-funnel advertising ROI](https://perion.com/blog/what-is-the-roi-of-full-funnel-advertising/) breaks down the classic brand-to-performance benchmark and how to recalibrate it for your category.


### How do I measure the success of top-of-funnel ads?


[Ad recall](https://perion.com/glossary/ad-recall/) , brand lift studies, and incremental reach – not last-click conversions. If a TOFU campaign is only ever reported on click-through rate, it’s being measured with the wrong ruler.


### Is full-funnel advertising relevant for B2B?


Yes, arguably more so than for B2C. B2B sales cycles run longer and involve more stakeholders, so the consideration and retention stages carry more of the total decision weight; a B2B brand that only runs BOFU search is competing for a tiny, expensive pool of buyers who are already deep in a cycle it never influenced.


### What is the biggest mistake brands make with the full-funnel advertising model?


Assuming “full-funnel” just means running more channels. The mistake that’s specific to 2026 is quieter: letting retention media get squeezed out by acquisition spend, so the funnel looks complete on a media plan but has no post-purchase stage in practice.


### How long does it take for full funnel advertising to show results?


BOFU results can show up in days. TOFU and retention compound over months, not weeks. For the full measurement-window breakdown by stage, see[our guide to the ROI of full-funnel advertising](https://perion.com/blog/what-is-the-roi-of-full-funnel-advertising/) .


### Can a small business run a full-funnel advertising strategy?


Yes, scaled down. A small business doesn’t need eight channels – one TOFU channel, one BOFU channel, and a basic retention list synced from a CRM cover all four stages. A local retailer, for example, might pair DOOH near its store with search retargeting and a simple post-purchase email or SMS segment, rather than trying to run CTV, audio, and social all at once.
